memory_update.text: AMKR should remain the US-listed reference OSAT anchor for memory/backend overflow, but its current market cap and rising AI attention make it less suitable as the main underfollowed alpha candidate.
FORM is a high-quality adjacent chokepoint candidate because HBM and DRAM growth directly increase probe-card complexity and demand; verify DRAM/HBM revenue concentration and margins in later layers.

KLIC is an underfollowed equipment-angle candidate for advanced memory packaging and backend expansion; survival in later layers depends on proof that memory/HBM tools are moving from product claims to material revenue.
COHU offers a smaller, more underfollowed HBM inspection/test-handler angle; its HBM revenue base is still small, so later-layer research must test materiality and repeat-order durability.

US-listed pure-play memory OSAT exposure is limited; many direct beneficiaries such as Powertech are Taiwan-listed, so the US universe is more weighted toward adjacent tools, probe cards, handlers, and inspection/metrology vendors.

node: Memory backend, OSAT, DRAM/NAND packaging and testing overflow
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around memory backend / OSAT overflow from the AI-HBM cycle. The cleanest US-listed reference anchor is Amkor, while the underfollowed lane is more attractive in adjacent chokepoints: probe cards for HBM/DRAM, bonding and advanced memory packaging equipment, and HBM inspection / test handlers. The key hypothesis is that AI-driven HBM demand raises utilization and urgency across memory packaging, test, inspection, and probe-card capacity, even for companies not usually treated as direct AI accelerator beneficiaries.
